decisive_finding.cause: terminate_and_reap sends process-group SIGTERM but returns immediately when the direct child exits, skipping group SIGKILL while another group member may remain alive.
decisive_finding.independent_probe: The actual run_confined timeout path produced descendant_alive_after_timeout=true for a child that exited on SIGTERM and a descendant that ignored SIGTERM.
decisive_finding.test_false_pass: The green timeout test manually sent process-group SIGKILL instead of exercising terminate_and_reap, so it could not detect the leak.
decisive_finding.impact: A fixture can retain a descendant beyond its immutable wall-time budget and escape process-lifetime/resource confinement.

required_correction: After the grace period, send SIGKILL to the process group regardless of whether the direct child already exited.
Reap the direct child without double-wait errors and verify no process-group member remains before reporting termination.
Exercise the actual run_confined or adapter timeout path with a descendant that ignores SIGTERM; do not manually substitute the kill sequence in the test.
Preserve CPU, address-space, file, sandbox/network, backend, collision, cleanup, and supplied-outcome behavior.
preserved_evidence: Exact 24-file and 20-owned identities, private visibility, and typed WorkerResult were independently verified.
The locked/offline 22/22 suite passes but the timeout test is insufficient for the claimed descendant guarantee.
claim_ceiling: No fixture resource-confinement acceptance, public HCT-FIXTURES, routine, strict, readiness, release, node closure, or completion.
no_claim_statement: This decision does not claim fixture behavior, public integration, readiness, release, node closure, or goal completion.
